summary: Implemented shared streamed JSON bounds, per-instance rate admission, health exemptions and fixed-category safe diagnostics with periodic operator logging.17 final focused cases and server typecheck pass;33 prior auth and9 focused upload/startup regressions also pass. Lead owns final integration.
limitations: Rate buckets and admission concurrency are per app/server instance, not distributed quotas. Direct peers behind an untrusted proxy share the proxy bucket; forwarded identities are deliberately ignored.
Defaults are configurable guardrails, not measured pilot capacity or production throughput claims. No production capacity/time-to-first-artifact baseline was measured.

The shared timeout bounds JSON reading. JSON/schema processing and application work are separately bounded by bytes and existing service policies; this does not claim a universal end-to-end request deadline.
Health/readiness are admission-exempt. Readiness retains its existing bounded shared storage probe.
run.queued is the most recent scheduler-observed queued row count for its connected database, with an observation timestamp; it can be stale and is not a process resource count.
No new HTTP diagnostic endpoint, proxy trust configuration, external telemetry export, full suite, browser run, build, live PostgreSQL, git action, deployment or delegation was used.

Exact hashes include whole shared app/server files at report time; only the assigned regions listed above were edited by this worker. Lead-owned diagnostic callsites and other concurrent M3 work need combined integration checks.
